newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese soldiers in Hong Kong get 900 pct pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Chinese soldiers in Hong Kong get 900 pct pay rise.

text.p: Chinese soldiers stationed in Hong Kong have hit the jackpot after Beijing decided to give them a payrise of 900 percent.

China has been forced to up the meagre salaries of troops based in the territory to help them cope with exorbitant living costs, the Weekly Digest said on Friday. It did not say when the wage hike would be implemented.

Soldiers garrisoned in the former British colony would receive a monthly wage of 500-600 yuan ($60-72), roughly nine times what their counterparts on the mainland receive, it said. The standard wage for soldiers on the mainland was a measly 60 yuan per month.

Commander of the Hong Kong Garrison Major-General Liu Zhenwu would also benefit from the rise with a paycheque of 12,000 yuan per month, while a lieutenant's monthly salary would be raised to 4,500 yuan, it said.
China has about 4,700 troops stationed in Hong Kong, which reverted to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
